symptoms: Diamond-shaped spots with grey centres and brown borders on leaves; neck blast on panicles.
treatment: Spray tricyclazole (0.6 g/L) or carbendazim (1 g/L) at first signs; repeat after 10-14 days.
prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, keep fields drained between irrigations.

symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules (stripes) on leaves that release powdery spores.
treatment: Spray propiconazole (1 mL/L) or tebuconazole as soon as pustules appear; repeat after 15 days.
prevention: Sow resistant varieties, early sowing, avoid late irrigation stress, rogue volunteer plants.

symptoms: Upward/downward curling of leaves, thickened veins, stunted growth, reduced bolls.
treatment: No chemical cure; control whitefly vector with imidacloprid (0.3 mL/L); remove and destroy infected plants.
prevention: Grow tolerant hybrids, rogue infected plants early, avoid cotton near old infected fields.

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves.
treatment: Spray mancozeb (2 g/L) or chlorothalonil (2 g/L) every 10 days during humid weather.
prevention: Crop rotation, stake plants for airflow, avoid overhead watering in the evening.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches on leaves with white fungal growth on undersides in humid weather.
treatment: Spray metalaxyl + mancozeb (2.5 g/L) immediately; remove affected plants if severe.
prevention: Use certified seed, avoid dense planting, destroy volunteer potatoes.

symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and stems, yellowing and leaf drop.
treatment: Spray wettable sulphur (2 g/L) or hexaconazole (1 mL/L) at first appearance.
prevention: Good air circulation, avoid excess nitrogen, sulphur dusting in early morning.

symptoms: Small circular brown/black spots with yellow halos that enlarge and merge.
treatment: Spray mancozeb (2 g/L) or carbendazim (1 g/L); repeat after 10-12 days.
prevention: Crop rotation, remove crop debris, avoid overhead irrigation.

symptoms: Yellowing along leaf veins, mosaic pattern, stunted fruit set.
treatment: No cure; control whitefly vector with imidacloprid; rogue infected plants.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties, remove alternate weed hosts, use yellow sticky traps.

symptoms: Window-pane damage on young leaves, ragged feeding, frass (sawdust-like) in whorl.
treatment: Apply emamectin benzoate (0.4 g/L) or spinetoram in the whorl; hand-pick egg masses.
prevention: Early sowing, intercropping with legumes, pheromone traps, biocontrol with Trichogramma.

symptoms: Holes in young bolls, damaged flowers, larval entry points with droppings.
treatment: Spray chlorantraniliprole (0.3 mL/L) at egg hatch; use pheromone traps for monitoring.
prevention: Timely sowing, intercropping, hand-picking damaged bolls, avoid late-season crop.
